risks: only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong downward trend (a net fall of ~154% of its level). There is little seasonal structure. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (1 points, ~0% of the sample). The series crosses zero, so percentage errors are unstable and mean-based combinations are safer than ratio-based ones. Across validation windows the model ranking is moderate (Kendall tau 0.429), which favours a weighted combination.

try a different weighted strategy that may handle high variance in error estimates – use softmax_neg_error weights.
trend_dominated and moderate ranking stability suggest a simple mean could compete; test a non‑weighted aggregate.
Use a trimmed mean to reduce influence of a few high-error models in a trend‑dominated series with moderate ranking stability.
Try a per‑horizon weighted strategy to capture model changes over the 24‑step horizon; the series is trend‑dominated but ranking stability is moderate, so per‑horizon weights may help.
test a dba (dynamic Bayesian averaging) on the full pool to see if it improves on the median baseline in a trend‑dominated series.
Test a weighted combination on the reduced pool4 with inverse_error weights to see if a smaller, less correlated set improves SMAPE, given trend-dominated regime and moderate stability.
test a per‑horizon weighted scheme on the smaller pool – softmax‑neg‑error may adapt to horizon‑specific strengths.
The series is trend dominated with moderate ranking stability; a simple non‑weighted mean over a focused subset may capture the trend better than weighted schemes that over‑emphasize outlier models.
Use a simple median aggregation on the smaller, high‑performing pool (pool4) to see if a non‑weighted robust mean can beat the weighted leader in this trend‑dominated series.
Test a weighted combination on the same pool4 but with a different weight handle (w4) to see if a different weighting scheme improves over the current best weighted w6.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w6' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.0832. Series context: trend strength 0.9002 and seasonal strength 0.183; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.429); 5 of 14 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 7726030196.79.
